ledger.note: 1124: the first listed reign. The page's table gives the legendary founder Mana Vikrama as 'reign 1124-?'; a Ramashwaram inscription of 1102 names 'Punthurakkon Manavikrama, the chief of Eranadu' (a title, not a founding date) and c. 1100 inscriptions use the title Punturakkon. The page is silent on the founding of Kozhikode and says the clan's original seat was Nediyiruppu. Calicut and its country are drawn as the core.

1405: 'the Perumpadappu ruler moved to Kochi in 1405 after Calicut took Thiruvanchikkulam' (Kodungallur). The page does not describe a Calicut conquest of Kochi with a date. [Reviewer sa-06-x, 2026-10-25: confidence lowered to 2: the Zamorin page dates to 1405 only the Perumpadappu ruler's move 'further south to Kochi'; it gives no date for the earlier shift to Thiruvanchikkulam or for Calicut's taking of it.]

1498: 'The Zamorin built a fort at Ponnani in 1498' (Vasco da Gama landed at Calicut that year); Ponnani's Thrikkavil Kovilakam was the clan's 'second home'. The page does not say when or from whom the Zamorin acquired Ponnani; it is drawn from this year as a bridge.

region.text: the Zamorin's lands: Calicut, Ponnani and Thiruvanchikkulam

ledger.note: 27 April 1766: Hyder Ali defeated the Zamorin and absorbed Calicut; the 117th Zamorin 'committed suicide' by fire ('Annexed by Mysore', table). The Mysorean invasion page has Hyder occupying Calicut, Valluvanad and Palghat in 1766 and making Faruqabad the local capital. A restored Zamorin prince, tribute to Mysore (1768 on the Zamorin page, not on the invasion page), the Company's occupations of 1782 and 1790 and the cession of Malabar to the Company in 1792 are not drawn; on 15 November 1806 the Zamorin became a pensioned landlord.

wars.name: Zamorin's wars with the Portuguese
wars.outcome: Intermittent war from the Zamorin's 1502 demand that the Portuguese factors leave Kochi to the peace sued for in 1540 by Chinna Kutti Ali, the Zamorin's admiral; the page names the 1526 siege of Calicut and gives no treaty year.
wars.note: The page dates 1502, 1526 (Siege of Calicut) and 1540; the years between are not given.

certainty.note: A coastal chiefdom with no surveyed frontier; the pages give places (Kozhikode, Thiruvanchikkulam, Ponnani) and a peak extent from Kozhikode Kollam to Panthalayini Kollam (Koyilandy) without a year, so every shape is a disc round those places.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks: cliopatria_names empty, three new keyframes. Two pages opened (Zamorin of Calicut, Mysorean invasion of Kerala); WebFetch returned extracts.

Evidence is thin on territory: the Zamorin page has no infobox, no founding year for Kozhikode, no area and no dated conquest except Thiruvanchikkulam (1405). The start year 1124 is the first reign the table lists (Mana Vikrama, '1124-?'), at confidence 1; the 1102 inscription and the title Punturakkon (c. 1100) are older. The page's peak extent ('from Kozhikode Kollam to ... Panthalayini Kollam (Koyilandy)', no year) is not a territorial claim that can be drawn. The valley of Valluvanad, Palakkad and the Eranad core around Nediyiruppu are not drawn (the page dates none of them to the Zamorin).

Disagreements: the Zamorin's end is 1766 (table, infobox-style) but the page also has a restored prince paying tribute to Mysore in 1768, the Company occupying Calicut in 1782 and leasing back the Zamorin's hereditary territory in 1792, and the pensioned landlord of 15 November 1806; the Mysorean invasion page is silent on the suicide and on the 1768 tribute. The dossier ends the state in April 1766 (the suicide, 27 April, is on the Zamorin page) and leaves the later Zamorin line to the notes.

Page silent / not drawn: the Portuguese fort at Chaliyam (1531, 1571), the Dutch-Zamorin treaty (11 November 1604) and the Dutch war (1753-1758 in a table), the defeat at Purakkad by Travancore (1755), the 1715-1717 Dutch and Cochin wars. Chinese fleets visited Calicut in 1407-1433 (trade, no land).

Cross-dossier: kingdom-of-cochin (the 1405 loss), kingdom-of-mysore (carries the 1766 gain under the name 'Zamorin of Kozhikode'), portuguese-india (the 1502-1540 war), east-india-company (Malabar 1792). Gazetteer: Ponnani and Kodungallur (Thiruvanchikkulam) are absent; discs at 75.93 E 10.77 N (25 km) and 76.20 E 10.23 N (22 km) are used.
